title: try to get rid of str(self) in proxy label mechanics once and for all

labels.name: great mcve

body:
**Describe the bug**
I've [recently hit a a breaking test](https://github.com/globality-corp/microcosm-eventsource/pull/74) in an open source library we maintain. 

The issue involves the use of`sqlalchemy.ext.compiler.compile` decorator.

We currently have two definitions of a function, one for a "default" dialect, and one specifically for postgresql (see [here](https://github.com/globality-corp/microcosm-eventsource/blob/develop/microcosm_eventsource/func.py#L67) for context):

```python
@compiles(last)
def compile(element, compiler, **kwargs):
    """
    By default, `last` is not defined.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError("last is only defined for postgresql")


@compiles(last, "postgresql")
def compile_postgres(element, compiler, **kwargs):
    """
    Define `last` in terms of the custom functions.
    """
    return f"last_agg({compiler.process(element.clauses)})"

```

Up to 1.4, this worked well enough - but since 1.4 it seems like having both definitions doesn't work: the sqlalchemy runtime seems to somehow pick up the "wrong" one (the default one rather than the postgresql one) when running our unit-tests.

If I simply remove the default one altogether, everything works fine. In `1.3.x`, this wasn't an issue however - I was able to have both definitions and have the sqlalchemy runtime use the right one everytime.

Is this intended behavior? any tips would be helpful, otherwise seems to me like a bug.

**Expected behavior**
Having multiple definitions for a function element `compiles()` block for different dialects should work as it did before `1.4` release.

**To Reproduce**

Please see [here](https://github.com/globality-corp/microcosm-eventsource/blob/develop/microcosm_eventsource/tests/test_func.py#L63) for unit-test which used to work and now fails. the actual code which is relevant is linked to above, for completeness here it is again:

```py
class last(FunctionElement):
    """
    Define a SQLAlchemy function that maps to a postgres function to select the last non-null value in window.
    """
    name = "last"

    @classmethod
    def of(cls, column, *filter_by):
        """
        Generate a window function over an event's column.
        """
        event = column.class_
        return cls(column).filter(*filter_by).over(
            order_by=event.clock.asc(),
            partition_by=event.container_id,
        )


@compiles(last)
def compile(element, compiler, **kwargs):
    """
    By default, `last` is not defined.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError("last is only defined for postgresql")


@compiles(last, "postgresql")
def compile_postgres(element, compiler, **kwargs):
    """
    Define `last` in terms of the custom functions.
    """
    return f"last_agg({compiler.process(element.clauses)})"

```

**Error**

See above, there is no explicit error message, rather the wrong specification is picked up by the runtime which doesnt match the active dialect when using `compiles()` on a `FunctionElement` class multiple times for different dialects.

**Versions.**
 - OS: OSX
 - Python: 3.8.1
 - SQLAlchemy: 1.4.x
 - Database: postgresql
 - DBAPI: psycopg2
